provenance.citation: Mitchell, T. M. (1982). Generalization as Search. Artificial Intelligence, 18(2), 203–226.
provenance.locus: The candidate-elimination algorithm (Sections 3–4) with the conjunctive attribute hypothesis language; the EnjoySport training sequence is the canonical worked instance of this algorithm (presented in full in Mitchell, Machine Learning, McGraw-Hill 1997, Ch. 2, Tables 2.1/2.5, which credits the 1982 paper).
provenance.notes: Four examples over six attributes (sky, airtemp, humidity, wind, water, forecast). Hand-derived boundary evolution: after the negative example 3, G3 has 3 members {<Sunny,?,?,?,?,?>, <?,Warm,?,?,?,?>, <?,?,?,?,?,Same>}; the final positive example 4 prunes the forecast hypothesis, leaving G4 with 2 members and S4 = <Sunny,Warm,?,Strong,?,?>.

input.intent: learn the EnjoySport concept by candidate elimination

expected.notes: S4 and G4 exactly as published; |G3| = 3 after the negative example.
